new.title: Two-sided characteristic cocycles on the exceptional coefficient resolution
new.statement: For \(y=v_-\) in degree nine at \(\tau=k+4=-3/2\), or \(y=z_+\) in degree twelve at \(\tau=3/2\), the original endomorphism algebra of the BRST coefficient functor admits explicit normalized regular-bimodule Hochschild cocycles in every arity. They have \(F_0=sO_y\), \(F_1(sQ)=-|y|\,sO_y\) and \(F_1(sT)=(-1)^{|y|}sO_{H_cy}\), where \(T=[Q,H_c]\). Both endpoint compositions occur. Graded commutativity and the absence of cohomology in the higher obstruction degrees suffice for these two generators.
hypotheses: Use the universal principal \(W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_4)\) and all smooth weak coefficients. In the negative raw ghost basis \(\delta_2=-\gamma_2/\tau\), the signed primitive deletes the spin-two letter with multiplier \(2/3\). Its first coefficient is \(122031\bmod 1000003\). On the positive fibre the specified vacuum-matter Cartan coefficients are exactly \(+1\) for \(a_+=h_{3,0}\) and \(-1\) for \(z_+\).

For the positive affine three-class, previously established fixed-fibre associative formality gives consistency of a \(31\times41\) system of rank nine. Two fixed diagonal minors have determinant \(+1\). Three arity-two and six arity-three native values suffice. Their numerical evaluations, a native cochain for the extra degree-eight class and identification of the separately normalized reduction maps remain open.

new.title: An independently normalized finite quantum measure on a nonflat meridian
new.statement: Two solid-torus Ward fillings agree near every face, corner and cut and have equal critical actions on each half. A fixed compact current and conjugate give bulk couplings \(B_1=1-i\epsilon,\ B_2=B_R=1\). Fix the two oriented input frames and independent half-densities. For one frequency-five meridian pair the sewn moment is \(Z_{j;k,\ell}=e^{-S_{\rm cl}/\hbar}\delta_{k\ell}(-\hbar)^k k!/(B_jB_R)\). At \(\epsilon=1/8\) the ratio of the two unnormalized vacua is \((64+8i)/65\) with phase \(\arctan(1/8)\). Sampling both dilation-related bulk supports exchanges the two diagonal couplings and gives ratio one.
hypotheses: Use \(q=1/2,\ \kappa\ne0,\ \hbar>0\), a common nonflat meridian, source-free exterior collars and the same oriented classical boundary primitives. The sources differ in disjoint interior patches in the left half. The fixed bulk contour is \(x=w,\ y=\bar w\). The negative-first Green pairing calibrates the seam, whose signed contour is \(b=-\bar a\).

For five frequencies \(2,\ldots,6\) use compact charges \(\pm17\), the product half-densities and the prescribed positive Virasoro identification, \(c>25\). If \(L\) is the collar width, the unnormalized ordered and projected stress values are \(Z_{\rm vac}\) times \(4ce^{-5L},\,14ce^{-5L},\,(62c/7)e^{-6L}\). The regulator is fixed before comparing the fillings. The full sourced boundary measure, its continuum limit and absolute cap phase are open.

new.title: A fixed quantum measure distinguishes two Ward fillings
new.text: On the \(q=1/2\) solid torus two fillings agree on collars of every boundary face and the nonflat middle meridian. Their classical actions agree on each half. Integrating the same compact current and conjugate gives left couplings \(1-i\epsilon\) and \(1\), with right coupling \(1\) in both preparations. At \(\epsilon=1/8\) the ratio of unnormalized amplitudes is \((64+8i)/65\). After vacuum division all signed one-mode moments agree. A symmetric regulator containing both interior tests gives ratio one. Five meridian pairs with independent Gaussian half-densities and the prescribed positive Virasoro marks give \(Z_{\rm vac}\) times \(4ce^{-5L}\), \(14ce^{-5L}\) and \((62c/7)e^{-6L}\). The compact cap still requires the measure on all modes and its regulator-removal limit.
